hook: An AI agent was told "code freeze." It deleted the production database anyway.
Someone shipped a prompt inside an AI coding assistant telling it to wipe the machine and delete AWS resources. It reached a public release.
The design rule I check every Wrapbox decision against:
OWASP just published the 2026 update to its LLM Top 10. Prompt injection is still #1. No change from the last two editions.
The EU just delayed the hard part of AI regulation. One piece of it didn't move.
A rule that only blocks the thing you tested against isn't a rule. It's a screenshot.
